newsitem.title: USA: US FCC head wants forward-looking antitrust policy.
newsitem.headline: US FCC head wants forward-looking antitrust policy.

text.p: The head of the Federal Communications Commission Thursday urged the government to adopt a forward-looking antitrust policy, given the rapid pace of change and mergers in the telecommunications business.

"We've got to lay out some path to the future for the businesses in this country," FCC Chairman Reed Hundt told a meeting of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, adding that the FCC could adapt the new thinking to its own role of clearing or rejecting mergers.
Hundt said the "traditional" ways of thinking about antitrust are not working very well.
He declined to speak directly about reported merger talks between AT&T Corp and SBC Communications Inc as well as mergers now pending before the FCC and future deals.

Hundt also said antitrust policy needs to be spelled out clearly so companies involved in the mergers and acquisition process have a better idea about what will pass government muster and what will not.
"We need to develop the parameters much more clearly. We need to articulate them much more clearly," Hundt said.
Hundt said there is a good deal of case law that "makes it clear" that the FCC's "public interest" standard for approving or rejecting mergers includes anti-trust considerations.
"In many ways I think our public interest standard is the canvas on which we have to write this 'information age' version of the potential competition theory," Hundt told reporters after his speech.
